chunks: Sahl, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, Umar ibn Yazeed, and Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated, saying:

A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) in Kufa and said, 'I have divorced my wife after she had become clean from her menstruation, before I had intercourse with her.' The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said, 'Did you have two just witnesses, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded?' He said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Go, for your divorce is not valid.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on divorce if there are no witnesses in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Shia juristic requirement of *shahadatayn* (two just witnesses) for the validity of *talaq*, distinguishing it from the Hanafi view where divorce is often effective by utterance alone. Imam Ali (peace be upon him) explicitly links this procedural requirement to the divine command in Surah At-Talaq, emphasizing that without witnesses, the divorce is considered null (*laysa bi-shay'*), even in the specific case of pre-consummation divorce after purity. This underscores the Shia emphasis on public declaration and evidentiary rigor in marital dissolution.

en.hubeali: Sahl, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Umar Bin Yazeed, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘A man came over to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> at Al-Kufa, so he said, ‘I divorced my wife after she was clean from her menstruation, before I slept with her’. So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Did you get two just witnesses just as Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic had Commanded?’ So he said, ‘No’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Go, for your divorce is not with anything’.
en.sarwar: 14. Sahl has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from ‘Umar ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“Once, a man in al-Kufah came to ’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and said, ‘I have divorced my wife after she became clean from her Hayd (menses) and before I went to bed with her.’ ’Amir al- Mu’minin asked, ‘Did you ask two just men to witness as Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has commanded to do?’ He replied, ‘No, I did not do so.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Your divorce in not valid.’”
